title.narrative: Support to the Implementation of the New Urban Agenda in Extremadura Region

description.narrative: The New Urban Agenda presents a paradigm shift and it lays out standards and principles for the planning, development, management, and improvement of urban areas along its five main pillars of implementation: national urban policies, urban legislation and regulations, urban planning and design, local economy and municipal finance, and local implementation. From these five pillars, national urban policies, plays a key role on the process of implementing the NUA, . National Urban Policies (NUP) are defined -with different names in different contexts - as a coherent set of decisions derived from a government-led process to coordinate and bring together various actors in order to achieve a common vision and objective, which promote a more sustainable, transformative, productive urban development, inclusive and resilient in the long term. A NUP provides the required coordination mechanism needed to promote equitable urban development. Implementing NUP could lead to enhanced local and national economic growth and ensure an equitable quality of life for all while protecting the environment. As a coordinating framework, NUP should not only be comprised of a list of corrective measures but also encourage proactive actions that foster economic, social and environmentally sensitive development. However, the definition and implementation of national urban policies in highly decentralized countries – such as the case of Spain and other federal countries-, where some or many of the urban planning competencies are not located at the central government level, may be compromised by other urban policies or strategies defined at other levels of government. The absence/weakness of mechanisms for the adequate effective coordination between the different levels of government in the implementation of urban policies and strategies, as well as the absence of incentives that promote cooperation between them, may constitute a barrier to the proper planning, management and development of cities and regions. In the case of Spain, a country with a high level of administrative decentralization, in recent years a high interest has been generated in the development of urban policies and strategies through the so-called "Urban agendas", which have been developed by the National Government and increasingly by the Regional Governments. However, the approval of these strategic instruments has not been accompanied by the development of an institutional framework that allows for proper coordination and governance, both in the definition processes and in the implementation phases. This Project focuses on the development of proposals that ensure coherence in the implementation of the New Urban Agenda through urban policies and strategies defined at different administrative political levels, in countries characterized by a high level of decentralization, in which different levels have competencies that must be coordinated and integrated. This project is part of the “umbrella” project “Implementing the New Urban Agenda in Spain through National and Sub-National Urban Agendas.” that it is being implemented since 2019 and groups different contributions from Spanish national and regional governments, that shares objectives and expected results. The General Objective of this project is to support the implementation of the New Urban Agenda in Spain through the promotion and establishment of urban agendas, policies and strategies at different levels of government. Specific Objective 1: to support national and sub-national governments in the definition and implementation of urban agendas, strategies and policies, and the development of implementing tools aligned with the urban dimension of the 2030 Agenda and the New Urban Agenda. Specific Objective 2: to promote the implementation of sustainable urban development solutions through advocacy, awareness and outreach activities related to the urban dimension of the 2030 Agenda and the New Urban Agenda. UN-Habitat and the Regional Government of Extremadura share the objective of cooperating in areas of mutual interest related to the New Urban Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals in cities, strengthening the capacities of subnational authorities and other partners to respond positively to the opportunities presented by urbanization, in order to transform cities into practical laboratories of multidimensional processes -economic, social and environmental- of sustainable development. Since 2019, UN-Habitat and the Regional Government of Extremadura have been working together on various initiatives with the general objective of promoting, in the Extremadura context and in the rest of Spain, the principles of sustainable urbanization, in the context of the 2030 Agenda for the Sustainable Development and the New Urban Agenda.
